Tomato Early Blight.local_summary: Early blight is characterized by dark brown concentric ring lesions ('target-spots') primarily on older lower leaves.
immediate_actions: Remove and safely dispose of severely spotted lower leaves to reduce spore inoculation.
Apply protective copper-based or chlorothalonil fungicide under dry conditions.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; apply water strictly at soil base.
preventive_actions: Implement a 3-year crop rotation avoiding Solanaceae family members.
Ensure minimum 60cm row spacing to promote air circulation and quick leaf drying.
Apply organic straw mulch around plant base to prevent soil splash.
monitoring_advice: Inspect lower leaves every 48-72 hours after warm rain or morning dew.
Re-scan symptomatic foliage within 3-5 days to measure lesion margin stability.

Tomato Late Blight.local_summary: Late blight is a destructive water-mold disease producing irregular pale green water-soaked lesions that rapidly darken, accompanied by white mold under leaves during humid weather.
immediate_actions: Immediately rogue and bury or bag infected foliage to halt rapid airborne zoospore dispersal.
Apply targeted systemic oomycete-active fungicide (e.g. Metalaxyl, Mancozeb) across entire field block.
preventive_actions: Plant certified disease-free transplants and blight-resistant cultivars.
Destroy volunteer tomato and potato cull piles within 500m of the field.
monitoring_advice: Daily scouting required under cool, overcast, high-humidity (>85%) weather conditions.
Rescan every 24-48 hours until spread is arrested.

Tomato Bacterial Spot.local_summary: Bacterial spot causes small, water-soaked dark circular spots (1-3mm) often with a chlorotic yellow halo. Lesions turn brown-black and dry out.
immediate_actions: Apply fixed copper bactericide paired with mancozeb to overcome copper tolerance.
Do NOT work in fields while foliage is wet from dew or rain to avoid mechanical spreading.
Sanitize pruning shears in 10% bleach solution between plant rows.
preventive_actions: Rotate out of solanaceous crops for at least 2 seasons.
Incorporate drip irrigation and avoid overhead sprinkling.
monitoring_advice: Monitor newly emerged vegetative flushes twice weekly during warm rainy periods.

Tomato healthy.local_summary: Leaf tissue exhibits vigorous chlorophyll density, uniform vein structure, and no visible lesions or parasitic chlorosis.
immediate_actions: Maintain routine balanced fertilization with adequate potassium and calcium.
Continue standard irrigation regimen based on evapotranspiration rates.
preventive_actions: Scout crop canopy weekly to preserve disease-free status.
Maintain weed-free field borders to eliminate insect vector reservoirs.

Potato Early Blight.local_summary: Foliar target-board lesions characterized by concentric rings on potato leaflets, causing premature senescence and tuber bulking reduction.
immediate_actions: Apply protective foliar fungicide (Mancozeb or Azoxystrobin) before canopy closure.
Maintain soil moisture to reduce physiological plant stress.
preventive_actions: Ensure proper nitrogen nutrition; stressed, senescing plants are most susceptible.
monitoring_advice: Scout mid-to-lower canopy every 5 days after tuber initiation.

Potato Late Blight.local_summary: Rapidly expanding necrotic water-soaked lesions on potato leaves with white sporulating margins under humid microclimates.
immediate_actions: Do not harvest infected tubers until vines have been completely desiccant-killed for 14 days.
preventive_actions: Hill up soil generously around stems to create a protective barrier against spores washing down to tubers.
monitoring_advice: Daily inspection during high-risk cool rainy spells.

Potato healthy.local_summary: Vigorous green potato foliage with intact cuticle and optimal photosynthetic health.
immediate_actions: Maintain regular pest scouting and balanced hilling schedule.
preventive_actions: Monitor soil moisture and maintain nutrient balance.

Pepper bell Bacterial spot.local_summary: Causes small, dark, water-soaked, blistering lesions on bell pepper leaves and fruit, causing severe defoliation in warm wet climates.
immediate_actions: Apply copper hydroxide plus mancozeb bactericide spray.
Never cultivate or harvest plants while foliage is wet.
preventive_actions: Practice clean field sanitation and drip irrigation.
